review_story.summary: A phone-filmed walk-through of a trading dashboard on a real laptop, followed by a selfie explanation. Nothing is screen-recorded or animated; the proof is a finger on a real screen.
review_story.hook: 0 to 5.6 s: the first shot is the dashboard itself, running on a laptop, with one small caption stating the claim. The face does not appear until 5.6 s.
highlights: The product is on screen for the first 5.6 s and for 13 of the first 18 s: the viewer sees the thing before hearing about it
The screen is filmed by hand with a finger pointing at rows (8.3 to 18.4 s), which reads as real in a way a clean screen recording does not
After the proof, one selfie take of 23 s is cut into five pieces: no b-roll, no graphics, the pace comes from the jump cuts
One static caption line at the top for the first 8 s instead of word-by-word captions
